title: How to Understand OpenTelemetry Signal Correlation
snippet: W3C Trace Context is the standard for distributed tracing propagation. When Service A calls Service B, it passes the trace ID in HTTP headers or gRPC metadata using W3C Trace Context format. Under OpenTelemetry and the W3C Trace Context specification, a trace ID is 128 bits, rendered as a 32-character hexadecimal string.

title: Trace ID Explained: What It Is and How It Works | Mastra Articles
snippet: Every distributed trace starts with a unique trace ID, a 16-byte identifier that follows the request through every service. OpenTelemetry uses W3C Trace Context by default. OpenTelemetry automatically propagates trace context across service boundaries using the W3C Trace Context standard, with every outgoing HTTP request, gRPC call, or message carrying a traceparent header that links child spans back to their parent.
claim: OpenTelemetry auto-propagates trace context via W3C traceparent header linking spans to parents.

title: How to Use OpenTelemetry Trace Correlation to Accelerate Root Cause Analysis
snippet: A correlation ID is a flat string meant for log search, while a trace ID anchors a structured tree of spans with timing data. In practice you can reuse the trace ID as your correlation ID, since it already propagates automatically and supports both log linking and latency analysis.
claim: Trace ID can serve as correlation ID for both log search and latency analysis in modern systems.
